title: ATO or compliance paperwork for new IRS mobile application

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: ATO or compliance paperwork for new IRS mobile application
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In the recent book "Blockers," the author Michael Lewis relays from Sahil Lavingia (now at the IRS) that he was able to build a new mobile app to replace IRS2Go. In the book, he relays that Sahil spent 2 months working on an application half time and just quietly replaced the official application. "It's just me on my own" is what he quotes Sahil Lavingia as saying.

Needless to say, this would be unusual if true. Every federal application deployed to production (including a mobile application talking to a backend) normally needs to get an Authority to Operate (ATO), which involves collecting evidence that the application conforms to NIST security controls as mandated by law in FISMA. There is an option for agency CIOs to sign a "Risk Acceptance Memo" (RAM) to bypass some of these requirements, but that would require coordination with the CIO.

I would like to request the following materials:
1. Any emails related to the launch of the new IRS application that replaced IRS2Go, either before it was launched or after. These can be limited to those sent to or mailed by Sahil Lavingia and Sam Corcos, or any other position at IRS who would be the Authorizing Official (AO) for this application launch.
2. An Authority to Operate (ATO) or related artifacts like a System Security Plan (SSP) or Security Impact Assessment (SIA) that would have been created as part of the pre-launch authorization to deploy this application to production. It is possible that this could have been created afterwards if the application was launched under a Risk Acceptance Memorandum.
3. Any listing of open areas where this new IRS mobile application is not in compliance with FISMA regulations. These are normally called (Plans of Action & Milestones) or POAMs. They would be around when an ATO was granted.
4. Any sort of Risk Acceptance Memo signed by an Authorizing Official (AO) who signed off on launching the application by assuming responsibility for risks that might impact the applications integrity, confidentiality and availability.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Harris

communications.communication:
Dear Open Records Coordinator,

I am writing on behalf of the Data Acquisition Lab to formally request access to public records under the Colorado Open Records Act § 24-72-201 et seq. We are requesting aggregated counts of student enrollment at the most granular geographic level available, which will enable a more meaningful understanding of community-level trends. We plan to request this information on a bi-annual basis going forward.

I am specifically requesting a tabular dataset containing the counts of enrolled students in Adams 12 Five Star Schools for the current 2025-2026 school year, disaggregated by the following fields:

- School identifier (name, NCES ID)
- Census tract GEOID (full 11-digit or abbreviated 6-digit code), census tract, or de-identified address
- Grade level
- Student enrollment count

Privacy Considerations:
- This request does not seek, nor does it require, personally identifiable information (PII) or any data points that could reasonably be used to identify individual students or households.
- We respect the importance of compliance with all applicable privacy laws. If additional thresholds or adjustments are required to ensure absolute privacy, we are happy to collaborate on refinements to the data as necessary.

If certain records or portions of records are exempt from disclosure, please provide a written explanation of the specific exemption(s) and release any non-exempt portions of the requested records. If this data is not centrally held, please advise which agency holds this data. Thank you for your attention to this request. If you have any questions or require further information, please feel free to contact me.

communications.communication:

communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).              A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;

             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.
